text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 2440 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS
- Prime Minister Gyula Horn has nominated Socialist MP Frigyes Nagy to replace the outgoing minister of agriculture. @

- National Police Commander Sandor Pinter Thursday told the ad hoc parliamentary investigating commission probing the Tocsik case that measures aimed at withdrawing the immunity rights of MPs may be deemed necessary in the near future.

- Budapest Police Commander Janos Bodracska was relieved of his day-to-day duties in a move seen as stemming from his failure to solve a recent spate of gang shootings and bombings. His powers have been extended to the entire territory of Hungary from December 1.

- Every second producer of dairy products may be facing bankruptcy along with several processing companies if no acceptable sales price can be agreed, warned Ferenc Berend, deputy chairman of the Dairy Product Council. @
- Transport Minister Karoly Lotz has dismissed Zoltan Rigo, CEO of the Hungarian State Railways. Rigo will be succeeded by Istvan Sipos, presently an operational director.
- The German holding company Siemens has bought 75 percent of the energy industry components manufacturer Erokar Rt.
- Price of Budapest public transport single fares will be increased from HUF 50 to HUF 61 from next January.
MAGYAR NEMZET @

- NATO Secretary-General Javier Solana told visiting Interior Minister Gabor Kuncze in Brussels on Thursday that Hungary will soon be officially requested to take part in the 18-month SFOR mission, set to replace IFOR in Bosnia in September.
- This paper learned that Minister of Labour Peter Kiss will supervise the Ministry of Welfare until a new minister is named.
- The Budapest Prosecutor's Office with immediate effect suspended the sale of Adolf Hitler's Mein Kamf.
NEPSZABADSAG @

- Speaker of Parliament told an international conference Thursday that there are prevailing concerns among the general public about the costs of admission to NATO, the stationing of foreign troops in Hungary and the deployment of nuclear weapons. Meanwhile, a poll shows that most Hungarians back NATO membership.
VILAGGAZDASAG
- An IMF delegation will arrive in Budapest next week.
- Hungarians must be forced to look after themselves in terms of saving for their pensions, said Finance Ministry State Secretary Tibor Draskovics. @

- Real wages in the private sector have stopped falling and the number of unemployed will not increase over the present 500,000, said Andras Vertes, managing director of the economic forecast firm GKI.
- Investors can submit their bids for a majority stake in the country's largest metals trading company Metallglobus by February.
MAGYAR HIRLAP
- Creditanstalt Security, New York Broker and ING Securities lead the list of Hungarian brokerages in terms of revenues in the first half of this year. @
- Bulgarian police officers struck, handcuffed and detained the Hungarian consul after two Hungarian businessmen locked themselves in the car and called the Hungarian embassy on their mobile phone.
-- Budapest newsroom (36-1) 327 4040
